q: How does waste heat power count in a Marmara cement plant's CBAM figure?
title: Cement waste heat power and CBAM
short: Waste heat recovery power uses heat from the kiln that is already counted, so it adds no fuel emissions. It lowers the grid electricity you buy, and with it the indirect emissions CBAM counts for cement. Meter its output separately.
audience: Cement plants in Turkey's Marmara region with waste heat recovery systems on kiln exhaust and clinker coolers

p: Cement is charged on indirect emissions as well as direct. Each kWh made from waste heat replaces a kWh from the grid at the country factor, so indirect emissions per tonne fall.

ul: Metered WHR generation and internal use.
Electricity per tonne of clinker and cement before and after.

p: The CBAM rules set how self generated electricity is valued. Confirm with your verifier how WHR output is treated in the version in force.
